habitat: Pairs in mixed bushveld, thornveld, valley bush, and riverine and coastal thickets, usually in the mid stratum. Not secretive, but often hard to locate.
summary: A common resident. Grey cap and mantle, olive-green wings and upper tail. The male has a yellow forehead, eyebrow and underparts, with orange only on the breast. That orange is much reduced in the female. The immature is only shown, not described. The call is a repeated poo-poo-poo-pooooo or pipit-eeez. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Olive Bush-Shrike’s black mask does not reach the bill. Its cinnamon morph is not limited to an orange breast patch, and its other morph is yellow below without that orange breast.

calls.description: A musical, much-repeated poo-poo-poo-pooooo or pipit-eeez, pipit-eeez. Grade A call from Mjejane Private Game Reserve, near Hectorspruit, Mpumalanga. The filename is XC323343-Shrike Orangebreasted Bush_Mjejane_160618_15_A.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The immature is only illustrated, so no immature variant is stored. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
